_meta.indication: INLYTA is indicated for the treatment of advanced renal cell carcinoma (RCC) after failure of one prior systemic therapy.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study A4061032 (AXIS), a pivotal randomized Phase 3 trial
pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Single randomized, open-label, multicenter trial comparing axitinib to sorafenib as second-line therapy; patients randomized 1:1 to axitinib 5 mg po BID or sorafenib 400 mg po BID. Protocol was granted an SPA.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with advanced/metastatic RCC with a clear cell component who had progressed after one prior systemic first-line regimen for mRCC; ECOG performance status 0 or 1.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Progression-free survival (PFS) as assessed by a blinded Independent Review Committee
pivotal_trials.result: Statistically significant improvement in PFS: median PFS 6.7 months (axitinib) vs 4.7 months (sorafenib); HR=0.67 (95% CI 0.54, 0.81); p<0.0001. ORR 19.4% vs 9.4%. No difference in overall survival (OS HR 0.97, 95% CI 0.80, 1.17).

nct_ctgov.title: Axitinib (AG 013736) As Second Line Therapy For Metastatic Renal Cell Cancer

key_safety: Most common (>=20%) adverse reactions: diarrhea (55%), hypertension (40%), fatigue (39%), decreased appetite (34%), nausea (32%), dysphonia (31%), palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia (hand-foot) syndrome (27%), weight decreased (25%), vomiting (24%), asthenia (21%), and constipation (20%).
target_moa: Axitinib is a kinase inhibitor that inhibits receptor tyrosine kinases including vascular endothelial growth factor receptors (VEGFR)-1, VEGFR-2, and VEGFR-3, which are implicated in pathologic angiogenesis, tumor growth, and cancer progression.

advisory_committee.vote: ODAC convened; in response to whether the benefit:risk evaluation was favorable for axitinib in advanced RCC after first-line failure, all 13 members voted "yes" (unanimous, no abstentions).

description.text: Added new indication for Inlyta in combination with avelumab or pembrolizumab for first-line treatment of advanced renal cell carcinoma

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for updates to the Inlyta Prescribing Information to include a new indication for use of Inlyta in combination with avelumab or pembrolizumab for the first-line treatment of patients with advanced renal cell carcinoma. This supplement also provides for updates to section 6.2 of the Prescribing Information in response to the Supplement Request letter dated May 21, 2020.

summary.text: Regular (full) approval of axitinib (INLYTA) for advanced RCC after failure of one prior systemic therapy, based on a statistically significant PFS improvement in the single pivotal randomized Phase 3 trial (Study A4061032); the NDA was presented to ODAC, which voted unanimously (13-0) that the benefit:risk was favorable.

citations.quote: Based on the findings described in this clinical review of the new drug application for axitinib (NDA 202324), this reviewer recommends regular approval of axitinib for the following indication:

A statistically significant improvement in PFS was demonstrated in patients receiving axitinib compared to patients receiving sorafenib (HR=0.67; 95% CI: 0.54, 0.81; p<0.0001, log-rank test). The median PFS of patients receiving axitinib was 6.7 months (95% CI: 6.3, 8.6) compared to a median PFS of 4.7 months (95% CI: 4.6, 5.6) for patients on the sorafenib arm. This improvement in PFS was greater in the cytokine-treated subgroup compared to the sunitinib-refractory subgroup. There was no difference in the final overall survival analysis between the two arms with a hazard ratio of 0.97 (95% CI 0.8-1.17). Please see table below.

Because axitinib is an NME, this NDA was presented to Oncology drug Advisory Committee (ODAC). In response to the question “Is the benefit:risk evaluation favorable for axitinib treatment in patients with advanced RCC after failure of a first-line systemic therapy?” All 13 members responded with a unanimous “yes” and there were no abstentions.
